_note: General agronomic guidance for the 38 PlantVillage classes. Chemical names are common active ingredients, not brands. Verify doses with the product label and your State Agricultural University / KVK recommendations before use. Edit freely; re-run scripts/seed_data.py to update the database.

diseases.description: Fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis, favoured by cool, wet spring weather.
diseases.symptoms: Olive-green to dark brown velvety spots on leaves and fruit; infected fruit becomes cracked and deformed.
diseases.treatment: Remove badly infected leaves. Spray a protectant fungicide such as captan or mancozeb at the label rate during wet periods, repeating as the label directs.
diseases.prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn, prune for air flow, and plant scab-resistant varieties.

diseases.description: Fungal disease (Botryosphaeria obtusa) affecting leaves, fruit and branches.
diseases.symptoms: Purple-bordered 'frog-eye' leaf spots; fruit rots with concentric dark rings; cankers on branches.
diseases.treatment: Prune out cankers and mummified fruit. Apply captan or another labelled fungicide from bloom onwards.
diseases.prevention: Remove dead wood and fallen fruit, and avoid wounding trees.

diseases.description: Rust fungus that alternates between apple and juniper (cedar) trees.
diseases.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surfaces, later with small tubes underneath.
diseases.treatment: Apply a labelled fungicide (for example myclobutanil) from pink bud stage when junipers are nearby.
diseases.prevention: Remove nearby junipers where possible and grow resistant apple varieties.

diseases.description: No disease symptoms detected on this leaf.
diseases.symptoms: Uniform green leaf without spots or lesions.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed.
diseases.prevention: Keep monitoring weekly, prune for air flow and keep the orchard clean.

diseases.description: No disease symptoms detected on this leaf.
diseases.symptoms: Uniform green leaf without spots.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed.
diseases.prevention: Maintain acidic, well-drained soil and monitor regularly.

diseases.description: Fungal disease (Podosphaera clandestina) common in warm, dry days with humid nights.
diseases.symptoms: White powdery patches on young leaves; leaves curl and may turn brown.
diseases.treatment: Spray wettable sulphur or another labelled powdery-mildew fungicide at first signs.
diseases.prevention: Prune for good air movement and avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer.

diseases.description: No disease symptoms detected on this leaf.
diseases.symptoms: Uniform green leaf.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed.
diseases.prevention: Continue routine monitoring and orchard hygiene.

diseases.description: Fungal disease (Cercospora zeae-maydis) favoured by warm, humid weather and maize residue.
diseases.symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular grey-tan lesions running between leaf veins.
diseases.treatment: If disease appears before tasselling on susceptible hybrids, spray a labelled fungicide such as azoxystrobin or propiconazole.
diseases.prevention: Rotate crops, bury or remove residue, and grow tolerant hybrids.

diseases.description: Fungal disease (Puccinia sorghi) spread by wind-borne spores in cool, moist weather.
diseases.symptoms: Small, raised, cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
diseases.treatment: Usually not needed on tolerant hybrids. On susceptible crops with early heavy infection, spray mancozeb or a labelled triazole fungicide.
diseases.prevention: Grow resistant hybrids and sow at the recommended time.

diseases.description: Fungal disease (Exserohilum turcicum) favoured by moderate temperatures and long dew periods.
diseases.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions on leaves.
diseases.treatment: Spray mancozeb or a labelled strobilurin/triazole fungicide when lesions appear on the upper leaves before silking.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant hybrids, rotate crops and manage residue.

diseases.description: No disease symptoms detected on this leaf.
diseases.symptoms: Uniform green leaf.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed.
diseases.prevention: Follow balanced fertilization and regular field scouting.

diseases.description: Fungal disease (Guignardia bidwellii) favoured by warm, wet weather.
diseases.symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots with dark borders; berries shrivel into hard black mummies.
diseases.treatment: Remove mummified berries. Spray a labelled fungicide such as mancozeb or myclobutanil from early shoot growth.
diseases.prevention: Prune for air flow, remove infected debris and keep the canopy open.

diseases.description: A complex trunk disease caused by several wood-infecting fungi.
diseases.symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' yellow or red bands between leaf veins; dark spots on berries; vine decline.
diseases.treatment: No curative spray exists. Cut out infected wood well below symptoms and protect large pruning cuts.
diseases.prevention: Prune in dry weather, disinfect tools and seal pruning wounds.

diseases.description: Fungal leaf spot (Pseudocercospora vitis) common in humid conditions.
diseases.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on leaves that merge; early leaf fall.
diseases.treatment: Spray copper oxychloride or mancozeb at the label rate.
diseases.prevention: Remove fallen leaves and maintain an open canopy.

diseases.description: No disease symptoms detected on this leaf.
diseases.symptoms: Uniform green leaf.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed.
diseases.prevention: Continue canopy management and weekly scouting.

diseases.description: Serious bacterial disease (Candidatus Liberibacter) spread by the Asian citrus psyllid. There is no cure.
diseases.symptoms: Blotchy, uneven yellowing of leaves; small, lopsided, bitter fruit; twig dieback.
diseases.treatment: Remove and destroy infected trees to protect healthy ones. Control psyllids with a labelled insecticide such as imidacloprid.
diseases.prevention: Plant certified disease-free saplings and monitor for psyllids regularly.

diseases.description: Bacterial disease (Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni) spread by rain and wind.
diseases.symptoms: Small angular water-soaked leaf spots that turn purple-black and fall out ('shot holes').
diseases.treatment: Spray copper-based bactericide at the label rate in early season.
diseases.prevention: Grow tolerant varieties and avoid overhead irrigation.

diseases.description: No disease symptoms detected on this leaf.
diseases.symptoms: Uniform green leaf.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed.
diseases.prevention: Continue routine monitoring.

diseases.description: Bacterial disease (Xanthomonas species) of pepper and chilli, spread by seed and rain splash.
diseases.symptoms: Small water-soaked leaf spots that turn brown with yellow halos; raised scabby spots on fruit.
diseases.treatment: Remove infected plants early. Spray copper oxychloride, alone or as the label allows, at 7-10 day intervals in wet weather.
diseases.prevention: Use certified or treated seed, rotate crops for 2-3 years and avoid overhead irrigation.

diseases.description: No disease symptoms detected on this leaf.
diseases.symptoms: Uniform green leaf.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed.
diseases.prevention: Keep scouting for spots, thrips and mites.

diseases.description: Fungal disease (Alternaria solani) that attacks older leaves first, especially in stressed plants.
diseases.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings ('target' pattern) and yellow halos on lower leaves.
diseases.treatment: Spray mancozeb or chlorothalonil at the label rate, repeating at 10-14 day intervals.
diseases.prevention: Rotate crops, use balanced fertilizer and remove infected plant debris.

diseases.description: Fast-spreading water mould (Phytophthora infestans) in cool, humid weather. Can destroy a field in days.
diseases.symptoms: Pale green water-soaked patches that turn dark brown; white mould under leaves in humid mornings.
diseases.treatment: Act immediately: spray a systemic + contact fungicide such as metalaxyl + mancozeb at the label rate; destroy badly affected plants.
diseases.prevention: Plant healthy seed tubers, earth up the rows, and spray protectively when cool, wet weather is forecast.

diseases.prevention: Watch closely during cool, humid weather for late blight.

diseases.description: Fungal disease of cucurbits, common in dry weather with humid nights.
diseases.symptoms: White powdery spots on both leaf surfaces that spread until leaves yellow and dry.
diseases.treatment: Spray wettable sulphur or another labelled fungicide (for example hexaconazole) at first signs.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant varieties, give plants space and avoid excess nitrogen.

diseases.description: Fungal disease (Diplocarpon earlianum) favoured by warm, wet weather.
diseases.symptoms: Many small purple spots that merge, making leaves look scorched.
diseases.treatment: Remove infected leaves and spray a labelled fungicide such as captan.
diseases.prevention: Plant healthy runners, avoid overhead watering and renovate beds after harvest.

diseases.description: No disease symptoms detected on this leaf.
diseases.symptoms: Uniform green leaf.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed.
diseases.prevention: Continue routine monitoring.

diseases.description: Bacterial disease (Xanthomonas species) spread by infected seed and rain splash.
diseases.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves, sometimes with yellow halos; scabby spots on fruit.
diseases.treatment: Remove infected leaves; spray copper oxychloride at the label rate in wet weather.
diseases.prevention: Use disease-free seed and seedlings, rotate crops and avoid working in wet fields.

diseases.description: Fungal disease (Alternaria solani) starting on older, lower leaves.
diseases.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric 'target' rings and yellow halos; leaves dry and fall.
diseases.treatment: Remove lower infected leaves; spray mancozeb or chlorothalonil at the label rate every 10-14 days.
diseases.prevention: Mulch, stake plants, rotate crops and avoid overhead irrigation.

diseases.description: Fast-spreading water mould (Phytophthora infestans) in cool, humid weather.
diseases.symptoms: Large greasy grey-green patches on leaves turning brown; firm brown rot on fruit.
diseases.treatment: Act immediately: remove infected plants and spray metalaxyl + mancozeb or another labelled late-blight fungicide.
diseases.prevention: Avoid planting near potatoes, keep foliage dry and spray protectively before forecast cool, wet weather.

diseases.description: Fungal disease (Passalora fulva) common in humid greenhouses and dense crops.
diseases.symptoms: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surface with olive-green velvety mould underneath.
diseases.treatment: Improve ventilation; spray a labelled fungicide such as chlorothalonil or mancozeb.
diseases.prevention: Reduce humidity, space plants well and grow resistant varieties.

diseases.description: Fungal disease (Septoria lycopersici) spread by rain splash from soil and debris.
diseases.symptoms: Many small round spots with dark borders and grey centres containing tiny black dots.
diseases.treatment: Remove infected lower leaves; spray chlorothalonil or mancozeb at the label rate.
diseases.prevention: Mulch to stop soil splash, rotate crops and remove crop debris.

diseases.description: Tiny mites (Tetranychus urticae) that suck leaf sap, worst in hot, dry weather.
diseases.symptoms: Fine yellow speckling on leaves, fine webbing underneath, leaves turn bronze and dry.
diseases.treatment: Spray water on leaf undersides to dislodge mites; if severe, use a labelled miticide such as abamectin or spiromesifen, or neem oil.
diseases.prevention: Avoid water stress and dust, and conserve natural predators by limiting broad-spectrum insecticides.

diseases.description: Fungal disease (Corynespora cassiicola) in warm, humid conditions.
diseases.symptoms: Brown spots with light centres and concentric rings on leaves, stems and fruit.
diseases.treatment: Spray a labelled fungicide such as chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin.
diseases.prevention: Improve air flow, avoid overhead irrigation and remove crop residue.

diseases.description: Viral disease spread by whiteflies. Infected plants cannot be cured.
diseases.symptoms: Upward curling, small and yellow-edged leaves; stunted plants with few fruits.
diseases.treatment: Uproot and destroy infected plants early. Control whiteflies with yellow sticky traps and a labelled insecticide such as imidacloprid or neem oil.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant varieties, raise seedlings under insect-proof net and remove weed hosts.

diseases.description: Highly contagious virus spread by hands, tools and infected seed. No cure.
diseases.symptoms: Light and dark green mottled (mosaic) leaves, leaf distortion and stunting.
diseases.treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants; wash hands and disinfect tools after handling them.
diseases.prevention: Use certified seed, resistant varieties and do not use tobacco while handling plants.

diseases.description: No disease symptoms detected on this leaf.
diseases.symptoms: Uniform green leaf without spots or curling.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed.
diseases.prevention: Scout twice a week, especially in humid weather.
